title: Four Sources of Pride
paragraphs: There is education where one learns about the world in a book and also the other kind where the world itself is the book to be read. Anybody excelling in both these types of education will naturally stand at the peak of knowledge. Such people had excelled in the past and do so at the present time as well. When the entire world showers praise upon them, we, as do these people, are filled with a sense of pride.
Those with an unflinching resolve with the flame of truth burning within can stand up to any challenge without fear. They are very brave indeed. Such people find a place among men of prowess.
With the golden saying, “If at all you live in this world, do so with fame” as their motto, people from all walks of life yearn for recognition and fame. Fame follows only those who don’t covet it.

It is the Koṅku land Where The women wear smiles bud-like That are sweet like mellifluous Tamiḻ Mixed with honey bees collect from flowers, And walk with a sense of pride Saying, “Even the tiny particles of food Carried by ants Are gifts from our king Kumaṇaṉ the munificent.”
Such is the emotion of pride as arising from the feeling that Kumaṇaṉ’s name is synonymous with liberality.
> The four sources of rightful pride are > Learning, prowess, unsullied fame and munificence absolute.
